newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, but outlook bearish.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, but outlook bearish.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Wednesday, consolidating after Tuesday's slump, but the outlook remained bearish, analysts said.
"Sloppy was how I'd describe the action today," Linnco Futures Group's Chicago trader Anthony Raia said.

"We saw fresh lows in gold and silver early, with some exchange-for-physical activity noted, but if key support levels around $380 in December gold and $4.80 in December silver break, we may see much lower levels," he said.
COMEX December gold ended down 30 cents at $381.30, after seeing an intraday low at $380.60.
Spot gold bullion ended quoted $380.15/380.55 an ounce, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $379.70 and the New York close Tuesday at $380.35/380.85.
COMEX December silver closed up 0.8 cent at $4.828 an ounce, after seeing a new two year low at $4.790.

After Wednesday's third quarter U.S. GDP data suggested the U.S. economy was slowing, U.S. bond prices climbed further to nine month highs, providing no incentive to investors to hold gold as an inflation hedge, analysts said.
U.S. third quarter GDP growth declined to 2.2 percent on an annual basis, down from 4.7 pct in the second quarter.
Meanwhile the ongoing rally in the US dollar to 42 month highs against the yen this week was slowing manufacturing demand for precious metals in Japan, analysts said.

"Your're getting down to some long term support on the charts, but there's clear weakness in silver with the December contract seeing the lowest levels in two years, and the last two days action in gold has put a damper on the past two week's rally from $380 in gold," Morgan Stanley analyst Rick Bensignor said.
"Central bank selling and producer hedging continues to hang over the market and will make it hard any substantial rally to occur," he said.
NYMEX January platinum settled up $1.70 an ounce at $385.50, after seeing fresh life-of-contract lows Tuesday.
NYMEX December palladium closed up $1.45 at $117.50 an ounce, after also seeing life-of-contract lows Tuesday.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
